title: "Hands-on: Degree Distributions and the Friendship Paradox"
---

Plotting a degree distribution badly is the most common mistake in network analysis. This notebook is mostly about not making it.

## What you will build

1. Generate a scale-free network and plot its degree distribution on linear axes, log-log axes, and as a CCDF.
2. Estimate the power-law exponent from the CCDF slope — and get the 1 - gamma correction right.
3. Demonstrate the friendship paradox by sampling edge endpoints rather than nodes.
4. Compare the degree distribution of nodes with that of their neighbours.
5. Identify hubs, remove them, and measure the damage.
6. Measure degree assortativity across different network types.

## What to watch for

- Compute the gap between your mean degree and mean friend degree, then check it against Var(k)/<k>. They should match exactly.
- Try the same plot with different bin widths. The PDF changes shape; the CCDF does not. That is the whole argument for the CCDF.
